page: Microsoft Azure D96as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, featuring 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs via two threads per core. The instance provides 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is present via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction set extensions, along with AVX support. Local ephemeral storage consists of an 825 GB SSD, and no discrete GPUs are bundled.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute capability and high memory subsystem performance. In stress-ng testing, multi-core CPU throughput reached 129,802.63, placing in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, complemented by a top-tier PassMark CPU encryption score of 103,065.31. Memory subsystem tests show high throughput for small-block cached operations at 6,005.62 GB/sec and a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,121.81. However, single-threaded processing remains in the mid-range, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,689.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth measuring 123.9 GB/sec.

The 96-vCPU scale and high parallel execution capacity offer strong resource density for enterprise software compilation, parallel compression tasks, and in-memory key-value stores, as evidenced by 89.06 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. The trade-off lies in moderate single-core instruction velocity and baseline uncached memory throughput. D96as_v4 is best suited for horizontally scaled multi-threaded enterprise workloads, relational and NoSQL database operations, heavy CI/CD build environments, and data transformation pipelines.

Multi-core performance is in the top tier, supported by top-decile stress-ng multi-thread results and high cryptographic test scores via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI extensions.
